summary: The Russian monarchy after adoption of the imperial title, expanding and governing territories across Europe, the Caucasus and northern and central Asia.
currency: Ruble, divided into 100 kopeks after Peter I’s monetary reforms.
rulers: Selected rulers: Peter I, emperor 1721–1725; Catherine II, 1762–1796.
economy: Peter’s military reforms stimulated industry and reorganized fiscal administration; economic conditions changed substantially over the empire’s two centuries.
military: The Great Northern War drove army reform and Baltic expansion; subsequent rulers pursued further territorial enlargement.
contributions: Imperial patronage developed major artistic collections and institutions, notably Catherine II’s collection that became the Hermitage.
origin: Peter adopted the imperial title after victory in the Great Northern War in 1721.
decline: The 1917 revolution overthrew the monarchy, ending imperial government and initiating contested successor regimes.
periodNote: 1721 marks adoption of the imperial title, not the beginning of the Russian state. Monarchical rule ended in March 1917.
